messages:

Cc: Karen Zhou <karen.zhou@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up + stakeholder map / procurement exception request

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the batching demo. Per our call, attaching the stakeholder map and the procurement playbook so you have our buying process on file.

A few asks from procurement: they typically require 60-day payment terms and our security team needs SOC2 evidence plus a confirmed data retention policy. Separately, we need an exception to standard pricing — our procurement lead asked if Redwood can provide a one-time onboarding discount and a 20% list discount for the first 12 months to make this work in our FY26 budget. They also asked about a 99.9% SLA for token throughput during business hours (their sales app is latency-sensitive).

Attached: acme-stakeholder-map.xlsx, procurement-exception-form.pdf

Can you confirm next steps and if any internal approvals are required on your side?

—Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Product Partnerships, Acme Corp

Looping you both in — Acme is asking for three things that will likely require approvals:

1) Pricing exception: 20% off list for first 12 months + onboarding credit (one-time).
2) SLA tweak: 99.9% business-hours token throughput SLA (higher than our standard for this tier).
3) Security/procurement paperwork: SOC 2 evidence and confirmation on retention/audit logs (they've attached the procurement form).

Aditya — can you advise on pricing authority / discount guardrails here?
Dev — any concerns about committing to a 99.9% token-throughput SLA at scale for their profile? If so, what mitigations (routing, dedicated pool) would we need to propose?

If we can get internal sign-off, I will respond with a conditional approval and propose a mutual action plan and timeline.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo follow-up + stakeholder map / procurement exception request

Thanks for the context — quick thoughts:

- Pricing: 20% is above my standard self-serve discount. For a deal of this size (roughly what we discussed on the demo — mid-six figures ARR run-rate), we can consider a time-bound 15% platform discount + $X onboarding credit. Anything beyond 15% will need Revenue Ops approval and a documented business case (net-new logo motion + reference potential).

- SLA: 99.9% token throughput is operationally significant. We can support that if Acme commits to a dedicated pool (Redwood Dedicated) or a reserved capacity slot and we define traffic shaping + burst policy. That will increase cost; we should tie the SLA to a specific capacity commitment.

- Security/procurement: SOC 2 and retention/audit logs — fine. We need to confirm whether they require on-prem key custody or additional contractual language (data processing addendum). If so, Legal will need to review.

I can approve a conditional 15% discount + $15k onboarding credit (subject to RevOps sign-off). I'll start a short internal ticket with RevOps and finance to get authority beyond that.

Aditya
Head of Sales Operations

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.com>, Karen Zhou <karen.zhou@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo follow-up + stakeholder map / procurement exception request

Marissa / Aditya — technical notes from infra:

- 99.9% business-hours token throughput SLA: achievable only with a reserved capacity plan. For the expected traffic profile Samir described, plan on provisioning a dedicated pool sized for peak qps + 20% buffer. We'll need a 30-day lead time for capacity provisioning (GPU ordering/config + testing) unless they accept a phased SLA (start with 99.0% for first 30 days, migrate to 99.9% post-provisioning).

- Security: SOC 2 evidence package is ready (SOC2 report v2.1). For retention/audit logs we can offer a 12-month standard retention; longer retention requires professional services (we can include as an add-on). If they need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), that's an enterprise Private deployment conversation.

I'm OK with the conditional SLA commitment provided we include the reserved capacity commitment in the MSA and tie the 99.9% SLA to that consumption commitment. Also recommend including automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in the event of capacity exhaustion to avoid full outages.

I'll attach the SOC2 summary and suggested SLA wording.

—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@acme.com>, Karen Zhou <karen.zhou@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Corp — procurement exception request & stakeholder map

Hi Samir / Karen — thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the stakeholder map. Internal alignment complete and next steps below: 

1) Pricing: We can offer a conditional 15% platform discount for the first 12 months + a $15,000 one-time onboarding credit. Any increase to 20% will require formal RevOps approval; if you can confirm projected ARR or reference-case impact it will speed that path.

2) SLA: We can commit to a 99.9% business-hours token-throughput SLA provided Acme signs a reserved capacity agreement (details below). Two options: (A) Reserved pool provisioned within 30 days, SLA effective after provisioning; or (B) phased SLA — 99.0% for first 30 days, 99.9% after capacity validation. Dev attached suggested SLA language and fallback policy.

3) Security/procurement: SOC2 summary is attached. Standard retention is 12 months; extended retention or customer-managed keying requires Private deployment add-on. Legal will prepare an addendum for the DPA/retention clause if needed.

Attachments: acme-stakeholder-map.xlsx, procurement-exception-form.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Related links: HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/ACME-2026-01 — I'll update with the conditional MA P (mutual action plan) and timeline. I will also upload the procurement-exception-form and route to RevOps for the formal pricing exception if you decide to pursue the 20% ask.

Next steps: 
- Samir/Karen: confirm which SLA path you prefer (A or B) and whether you can commit to the reserved capacity sizing (we can share a recommended capacity number once we have QPS estimates).
- Procurement: confirm required contract language for retention/KMS and whether DocuSign is preferred (we can prepare).

Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful — propose Thu 26 Mar 10:00 PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
